chunk_findings.detail: The added validator references `SECURITY_DISCLOSE` on the line `if "disclose" in t and t["disclose"] not in SECURITY_DISCLOSE:` and in the error message, but this diff adds only `SECURITY_TABLE_KEYS` and no import of `SECURITY_DISCLOSE`. Therefore loading any `[export.security]` table (for example `disclose = "ids"`) makes `_export_table_problem` call `_security_keys_problem` and raise `NameError` instead of returning a validation message, so the security export config cannot be validated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/export.py:_security_keys_problem

chunk_findings.detail: `collect` only returns `versions`, `open`, and `fixed`. It never queries security-pass findings or dependency-advisory data, so a recorded security finding, or an unfixed dependency advisory with no matching `Bug`, is absent from the generated SECURITY.md Known Issues and vulnerable-version marks. The intended change requires known issues from open/fixed security-tagged bugs and the security pass, and vulnerable versions for unfixed dependency advisories; this data function makes that impossible for the SECURITY doc type that reuses it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:collect

chunk_findings.detail: `_versions` identifies the current release line by absolute newest git tag: the first row inserted gets `newest=True` because of `not rows`. If an old maintenance line receives a backport tag after the newer major release (for example `1.5.9` tagged after `2.0.0`) and `1.5` is not in `cfg.flow.lines`, `_status` still returns `"supported"` for `1.5`. SECURITY.md then marks an EOL/old line as supported even though only the current release line should be supported by default.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_versions

chunk_findings.detail: The new `target_of` probes the filesystem directly with `(Path(repo) / rel).is_file()` instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, violating [r-adapters] (“filesystem layout” must use an adapter so tests and swaps touch one place). A concrete failure: if an `also_at` directory such as `repo/.github` exists but is unreadable, `Path.is_file()` can raise `PermissionError` and crash refresh/status even when the actual target `spec.path` exists and would have been used directly; an adapter-backed filesystem check would keep that behavior isolated and testable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:target_of

chunk_findings.detail: When an existing CRLF file lacks a region and `force` is true, `_appended` builds each region with `render_region(doc, n, bodies[n])`; that embeds the `body-sha256` of the LF body from `rendered`, and only afterwards converts LF to CRLF in the whole block with `.replace("\n", eol)`. The appended region's body bytes in the file are then CRLF while its `body-sha256` marker hashes the LF body. Example: a CRLF `SECURITY.md` without the managed block, when exported with `--force`, gets a block whose body hash does not match its body. The next non-force refresh sees that mismatch as a hand-edited region and refuses to update it (or reports drift), so the file does not stabilize after the operator confirms the append.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py:_appended

chunk_findings.detail: The known-issues section ends with “Dependency advisories and security-pass findings are not recorded there, so they are not covered here.” This contradicts the stated intent that the known issues must include “findings of the security pass,” and the requirement that a version carrying an unfixed dependency advisory be marked vulnerable. Given a security-pass finding, the generated SECURITY.md will either omit it while falsely claiming it is not covered, or list it while the text says it is not, making the exported security policy inaccurate. The same omission is echoed in ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md, which says known issues come only from bugs tagged `security` or `secbug`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2

chunk_findings.detail: The test helper `git()` invokes `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], ...)`, a direct external subprocess tool. This violates [r-adapters], which requires every external dependency (including git and subprocess tools) to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. The new test file therefore introduces an out-of-adapter dependency in the change.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_security.py:git

chunk_findings.detail: In `ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2`, the `known-issues` region wraps both the `open` and `fixed` loops inside an `{% if open or fixed %}` check, but the closing `{% endcall %}` is placed *after* the explanatory text ("These are the bugs recorded as security issues..."). When both `open` and `fixed` are empty, the template falls through to `{% else %}` and renders "None recorded." inside the region, but because the explanation follows the `{% if %}` block and is outside it, an empty project will render the "None recorded." line *followed by* the explanatory text saying "These are the bugs recorded as security issues in this project's log...", which is contradictory and misleading since no bugs are recorded at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2:23

data.reason: the review was terminated by SIGTERM before a reviewer finished: nothing was reviewed, which is not a pass

data.body: B-export-security-md shipped `ddflow export security` from recorded bugs and version tags only, because nothing else is recorded yet, and the document says so. Left for this task, from that task's body: (1) dependency advisories and security-pass findings have no record to read; once SEC-findings turns findings into bugs, tagged ones appear by themselves, so check what remains (an unfixed advisory marking a version) and drop the 'not covered' sentence from the template; (2) refresh triggers: [export].refresh has merge, phase_close and docs_gate, so a dependency-upgrade merge and document maintenance are covered, but a version cut and a security pass completing are not (a cut must render the tag it is about to make, as services/changelog_cut.py does); (3) a policy found at .github/ or docs/ is not the path `Config.export.targets()` reports, so the lease shared-path list and the region pre-commit check see SECURITY.md unless [export.security].path is set: core cannot look at the repo there.
data.title: SECURITY.md follows the security pass: findings and dependency advisories in kind_security, refresh on version cut and security pass
